items.note: The plan states the forward invocation y_S <- y_S + x_S for arbitrary scratch and the three-stage (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) exchange, and the method gives the remove/use/restore schedule. It never names the copy/gather/scatter/side-injection gates on triples, or why (JV+RG)x is the identity (central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2 or (|S cap T|-1)/2, cancelled by side wires, lines 752-759). It also omits the wire counts.

It states D_out S D_in^{-1} and the route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}. It derives them as the paper does (lines 804-822), by the stored = frame(logical) invariant, which holds at sources by definition and passes through gates by linearity.

S1.3.1 states the lemma: comparable nondegenerate labels, central 3->4 edges as the only losses of h each, sum |Delta dim| = Wm-2N+2L with L<N/2. It does not give L=Ich or the ratios 100/539 and 101/539. The method gestures at tensor labels and a residual table but omits the bilinear form x^T(I-J/9)y (or F_2 dot product) that makes neighbouring triple lines orthogonal. That orthogonality is the key to the side-wire inclusion. It also omits the signed-sum telescoping (sources N, sinks Wm-N) and the orthonormal-basis argument over F_2.

It gives P_U at gates and sinks, -P_{U_a} at X_a sources, endpoint difference I_m, s<Wm, and (in S2.2.2) the frames Phi_M producing H <- H+D. It never writes s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b; this follows only by combining S1.3.1 with the S1.3 method's remark about N extra ranks. The rank(P_V-P_U) = dim V - dim U argument and the computation P_{U_a^perp} + P_{U_a} = I (lines 1158-1171) are not shown.

The route follows the proof closely: weight additivity mod 4 for orthogonal vectors, i^{eps[v.x]} turned into aI+bX_v via H diag(1,-1) H = X, telescoping, and the X_a->Y_a repair via C=iZC^{-1}Z on 27 coordinates. The statement gives only s<Wm, not s_c = W_c m - 2N + 2L_c. Undoing the signed exchange is not mentioned.

s<Wm (S1), s/W<m^tau with tau<1 (S2.2) and tau=sigma=1-2^{-50} (S7.1) appear. The relative deficits eta_b, eta_c, the bound eta > 20*2^{-50}, and the log m<20 argument giving s/W<m^tau are absent. Nothing ties L<N/2 to the strict saving beyond the S1.3 method remark.

Controlled shifts, unit multiplications, cyclic row splitting and splitting on a bit are used as linear-time tools, but neither lemma's content (the O(V) operations and the condition that the offset is computable in b^{O(1)}) is stated.

The factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 (topmost row, rightmost pivot elimination), the O(V) lower triangular transforms and the one-interchange realization of each one of Pi all match lines 1375-1446. The choice of a fixed odd prime q avoiding all denominators and diagonal numerators (lines 1413-1423) is omitted. That choice is what lets the rational identities hold over Z/q^b; I count it as essential, conservatively.

Every step of the proof is present: cyclic row split into W role streams of volume V/W, Phi_M frames with endpoint I_m, the three-shear interchange, s recursive calls, F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) by geometric sum, and the depth-first parking schedule.

Matches the proof: rho = O(log) high digits form the row field (padding to a multiple of W^k), base-m pieces go to power-width calls summing to O(Ve^tau), and binary ranges are padded to [q^e]. The unequal-width extension (lines 1740-1762) is not covered, but it is an add-on, not part of the lemma's proof.

It has the row-addition count, s child calls on f axes with inverses from forward calls, and H_0^{otimes D} = b^D S_D C^{otimes D} S_D. It never states the conjugation P_M X_v P_M^{-1} = X_{Mv} that moves residual directions onto coordinate slots (eq:phase-edge-coordinate), which is the reason for the binary change of basis. The inverse-child identity (C^{-1})^{otimes f} = (-i)^f Z C Z is asserted without its formula.

It has the eight conditional additions restoring w, the bad-set fraction 80(f-1)2^{-K}, repair by extraction and radix sort, and the family cost O(V(L^tau+1)). The method never says that each rotation needs width-L chunk swaps to move its target behind its controls (lines 2117-2155), which is where the L^tau term comes from. It also does not note that T_0 S_0^{-1} permutes only the bad set.

It gives node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)), rows from the first chunks split u=Wg+w with V/W children, and F(e) <= (s/W)F(e/m) + O((eK)^tau+1). It omits the leaf cutoff e<d^beta, the bound K <= e^{c/beta} making the overhead O(e^lambda), the base-m piece decomposition, and the condition max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)} < lambda'. S3.8 attributes the result only to s/W<m.

It has O(Vd^{lambda'}) cost, exact evaluation with one final truncation, and error < sqrt2 2^{-p} via absolute row sum one. The statement drops K=floor(d^c) and the parameter conditions. The guard-width step only asserts a fixed power of d without the depth recurrence A(e) <= sA(e/m)+E or Delta = ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) with epsilon C_1 < 1.

It covers character cancellation, decimation in frequency, bit-reversed storage B_t F_t^- and F_t^+ B_t^{-1}, grouped rounds H then J_E, the layout L, one truncation per round via oddness of Q_p, the error sqrt2 ell 2^{-p}, and the cost O(Tp[dK+pK^{tau-1}+ell d^{lambda'}]). S4.2.1 misattributes a cost (listed under errors).

Follows the proof: B_0 = 2^{4p}, four products of evaluation integers by the HvdH multiplier, centered residues with carry in {0,1} using |h_j| <= r2^{2p} < B_0/2, reduction mod y^r+1, and shift by p+ell, giving Q_p(fg/r) in O(rp log(rp)).

It gives the common LB order, M pointwise packed products, the opposite transform and scaling by M, the normalization through F^-(f*g) = M F^-f F^-g and F^+F^- = I/M, and the error sqrt2 M(3ell+1)2^{-p} by bilinear contraction, all as in the paper.

It has the Gaussian maps S, T, selection C, diagonal D, ||N-I|| < 2^{-alpha^2 theta}, the Neumann inverse, A=S' and B_0 = D'J'C giving P_sF_s = 2^{2alpha^2} B_0 P_tF_t A, the tensor form with gamma=2d alpha^2, the linewise padded-box implementation, and the axis-exposure cost.

It gives the chirp's period and coefficient check for QF_t, the dilation identity F^+R_c = R_c^{-1}F^+ giving RF^+R = F^+, commutation with pointwise products, and the normalized convolution rule giving (u*v)/S^2. The conjugation remark for RF^+ is not in S6.

It gives tau, sigma, epsilon, kappa, the sizes b, p, d, K, T, r, Tp = Theta(n), the prime-interval count, T/2<S<T, and no wraparound with c_j < 2^{3b}. Missing: the values of lambda, c, lambda' and delta; eta = 1/(4d); alpha = ceil((12d^2 b)^{1/4}) and gamma bounds; and the check alpha^4 theta_i > p, which the plan only claims as enough separation.

It has the isomorphism (image of x has order S), the triangular b_i formula, updates i=d..1 from original digits after reordering axes, zero padding preserved, an explicit inverse, and cost O(Tp d^2(1+ell^tau)).

The exact isometric isomorphism, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h = zeta^j, and M_C = D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g) = (f*g)/T are derived. The computed version (twist factors with error < 2 2^{-p}, truncated phase products, format normalization, lines 4349-4413) is not covered.

Its steps match the six-step algorithm, the source transform A, chirp, B_0, 2^gamma with counterpart RF_s, and the explanation of the two scales by S. Two things are not stated: the digit scaling 2^{-b-2} (only implied by the 2^{2b+4} rescale) and the definition of the opposite procedure by complex conjugation.

It has the contraction error propagation, E_ring < 5TL, chirp < 8TL, E_s = 9 2^gamma TL with norm < .501, (3E_s+2) for the opposite transform, the final 448b 2^{-3b/4} < 1/2, unique rounding and the carry invariant, as in the paper. E_w and gamma <= b/4 are not written out.

The route matches: normalize by V=Tp, seven margins with minimum 2^{-181} = 2kappa, setup and exceptional streams o(V), log powers <= p^kappa, and a schoolbook cutoff. The seven normalized cost terms and the margin formulas (e.g. g_2 = epsilon c(1-tau)) are not listed, although the costs appear scattered in S4 and S5.
S0 says the bound refutes the n log n optimality conjecture in this model. It does not give the eventual-lower-bound formulation or the liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n) = 0 argument.

errors.says: Moving the O(dK) low-order bit slots to a prefix and exchanging at most dq chunks places chunk j of all axes consecutively at cost O(Tp pK^{tau-1}).
errors.paper: The prefix list also includes the top slot (i, ell-1) of each long axis. The slot moves cost O(TpdK) and the chunk exchanges alone cost O(Tp pK^{tau-1}); these are separate terms of the transform cost.

errors.says: The packed shifts agree with the intended XORs except at addresses whose guard values lie within 20 of the segment boundary.
errors.paper: The excluded set is where a guard value g fails 10 <= g <= 2^{K-1}-11, i.e. guards within 10 of their range ends. It is the K-bit segment values that then lie in [20, 2^K-21].

chain: The tree follows the paper's route from the scalar exchange network and frames, through the two interfaces, the interchange and layer recurrences, the synthetic transforms, resampling and chirp, to the assembled algorithm, error bound and cost tally. It reaches the O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) bound with almost no misstatements. It is thinnest where the power saving is made: the label construction lacks the bilinear form and the orthogonality of neighbouring triples, s/W < m^tau is asserted without the deficits eta and the log m < 20 step, and the layer recurrence and guard widths are stated without their unrolling conditions. The final cost table is also only summarized.
